cs.label: [section] Cíl předmětu a studijní výstupy:
cs.content: How can one comprehend, analyse, and interpret the ongoing crises and political affairs in the world? Comparative Politics in Use is an elective and language-focused course compounded of selected political matters and its connexion to political science, international relations, and area studies. The course has been primarily designed for non-native English speakers, and accordingly, it shall endeavour to clarify and elaborate on sundry political phenomena. And afterwards, one shall know how to put it into practice in the form of political research as, for instance, in BA and/or MA theses. This course has been set up for students to help them achieve the following: * Acquire a working knowledge of modern history and politics; * Ability to discuss and analyse the contemporary affairs of the area in English; * Improve communication and writing skills. Due to the structure of this course, however, it is imperative that one is in possession of at least the B2 level of English (CEFR) in order to understand and communicate in class. No certificates proving the level of English are required, though. The course highly encourages the students to become familiar with and capable of engaging with manifold cruces in politics. And since this is a sphere of swift changes, so it is indispensable to keep abreast of current affairs. Hence, all the students are advised to follow and read, for instance, The Economist and The Financial Times on a regular basis, whilst other press may remain upon one's preference and liking.
